title: F.batch_norm accepts illegal negative epsilon values and produces inconsistent NaN (CPU) vs inf (CUDA) results
bug_description:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

API bug: batch_norm lacks input validation for epsilon parameter, allowing mathematically invalid values
BUG: batch_norm should reject eps <= 0 but instead produces platform-dependent undefined behavior
Input validation missing: batch_norm permits mathematically invalid negative epsilon values

### code
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
torch.manual_seed(42)
torch.cuda.manual_seed(42)
input_tensor = torch.tensor([[[[1.0]]]]) 
running_mean = torch.zeros(1)
running_var = torch.ones(1)

cpu_result = F.batch_norm(input_tensor, running_mean, running_var, eps=-1.0)
cuda_result = F.batch_norm(input_tensor.cuda(), running_mean.cuda(), running_var.cuda(), eps=-1.0)
print(cpu_result,cuda_result)

### output
tensor([[[[nan]]]]) tensor([[[[inf]]]], device='cuda:0')
